question.text: An offshore Mauritius fund uses an Indian investment adviser to source deals. What is the principal tax risk if this relationship is poorly documented?

answer.text: The offshore fund will lose its SEBI FVCI registration automatically.
The 'Place of Effective Management' (POEM) of the offshore fund may be held to be in India, subjecting its global income to Indian tax.
The Indian adviser will be deemed the GP of the offshore fund.
Mauritius will impose 30% withholding tax on all distributions.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** If the Indian adviser effectively makes investment decisions, Indian tax authorities may hold the offshore fund's POEM is in India, making it a resident for Indian tax purposes - which would tax its global income in India, destroying treaty benefits. **The Trap:** FVCI loss has no automatic link. GP-deeming is fabricated. Mauritius withholding claim is invented. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C Ch 13 taxation tests POEM. XIX-A distributors may see it in cross-border suitability questions. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Always sign an 'advisory-only, non-binding' engagement letter with the India adviser and explicitly document that investment decisions are made offshore - this preserves the offshore fund's non-resident status.
